university: University of Colorado Denver/Anschutz Medical Campus

documents.unit: Student Conduct and Community Standards, CU Denver
documents.title: GenAI and Academic Integrity
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single rule. It says authorization "is legitimate only if given by the faculty member", that students must "check with your faculty about AI use in their course", and that rules "may vary for each assignment"; it offers an AI Assessment Scale of four levels. A tiered, instructor-decided scheme makes the stance delegates, even though the fallback is "assume you DO NOT have permission".
documents.summary: CU Denver Student Conduct explains how the Academic Integrity Policy (7050) applies to generative AI: AI-completed work is likely cheating, uncredited AI work is plagiarism, and inaccurate or altered AI output can be fabrication or falsification. Faculty decide what is allowed, using a four-level AI Assessment Scale, and a student checklist covers ownership, verification, citation and ability to explain the work.

units.why: The page opens by binding every student to Campus Policy 7050: "All students are held to the University's Academic Integrity Policy". This is a compliance-with-existing-policy rule (P77), not a collaborator analogy (P45).
units.anchor: All students are held to the University's Academic Integrity Policy

units.why: "we expect ethical use of Generative AI" states a community expectation about AI in academic work. P95 (integrity culture of the community) fits better than P56 because it gives no purpose or scope, only an ethical expectation.
units.anchor: As a community we expect ethical use of Generative AI (GenAI) in your academic work

units.why: The cheating definition says "Authorization is legitimate only if given by the faculty member", so the instructor alone decides what AI is authorized (P04). It is a decision-rights rule, not a tier list.
units.anchor: is legitimate only if given by the faculty member responsible for the evaluation

units.why: "Prompting Generative AI (GenAI) to complete a task, that has been assigned to you by a faculty member, is likely cheating" classifies AI-completed work as misconduct, so P36. P19 also fits but the sentence's load-bearing move is the cheating label.
units.anchor: that has been assigned to you by a faculty member, is likely cheating
units.fit_note: Also says students may not have AI complete assigned tasks (P19); filed under P36 because it labels the act cheating.

units.why: "By asking GenAI to do your work, your faculty member is unable to evaluate your learning" gives the reason for the ban as honest evaluation of learning. P95 (honest evaluation) rather than P41 (skill-building practice) because the stated harm is to evaluation.
units.anchor: your faculty member is unable to evaluate your learning

units.why: "unless you have expressed permission from your faculty member, assume you DO NOT have permission to use GenAI" sets the default when no permission is given, so the fallback rule P06.
units.anchor: assume you DO NOT have permission to use GenAI

units.why: "Submitting work completed by GenAI without giving this source credit is plagiarism" makes failure to credit AI the violation. P28 (nondisclosure is the violation) fits better than P36 because the trigger is missing credit.
units.anchor: Submitting work completed by GenAI without giving this source credit is plagiarism

units.why: "Making slights edits and changes to a GenAI output is considered mosaic plagiarism" classifies lightly edited AI output as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: Making slights edits and changes to a GenAI output is considered

units.why: "You are responsible to find, ensure they are valid, and cite the original sources" tells students to verify and cite the original sources behind GenAI output. P31 (verify) is chosen because the main duty is validity; citing sources partly exceeds it.
units.anchor: You are responsible to find, ensure they are valid, and cite the original sources
units.fit_note: Also requires citing the original sources behind AI output, not only verifying them.

units.why: The MLA line gives the form of a ChatGPT citation: prompt text, version, OpenAI, date accessed, URL. That names tool, prompt and date, so P25.
units.anchor: prompt. ChatGPT, Version, OpenAI, Date accessed, URL
units.policy: Students cite ChatGPT in MLA format as: prompt text, ChatGPT, version, OpenAI, date accessed, URL.

units.why: The APA line gives the form of a ChatGPT citation with author, year, version and URL. It is a second citation format, so P25 again.
units.anchor: OpenAI. (2023) ChatGPT (May 3 version)[Large language model]. URL.
units.policy: Students cite ChatGPT in APA format as: OpenAI. (2023) ChatGPT (May 3 version) [Large language model]. URL.
units.fit_note: Gives the APA format (tool, version, year, URL) but not the prompt.

units.why: "Submitting work that is factually inaccurate from GenAI could be seen as a fabrication of information" classifies inaccurate AI output as a misconduct (fabrication), so P36.
units.anchor: factually inaccurate from GenAI could be seen as a fabrication of information

units.why: "GenAI is known to produce hallucinated sources and results" is a fact that warns output is unreliable, so P31 with modality informs.
units.anchor: GenAI is known to produce "hallucinated" sources and results.

units.why: "Using GenAI to forge documents may also be a violation of the Student Code of Conduct" is a conduct rule against using AI to falsify records, so P74.
units.anchor: GenAI to forge documents may also be a violation of the Student Code of Conduct

units.why: "you are responsible to determine the validity of all sources that you use in academic tasks" puts verification on the student. P31 because it is a verify duty.
units.anchor: responsible to determine the validity of all sources that you use

units.why: "Instructing GenAI to alter, change, or skew results may be considered falsification" bans using AI to falsify data. P74 (falsify data) fits its definition; it is also misconduct (P36) but the act described is falsification.
units.anchor: Instructing GenAI to alter, change, or skew results may be considered

units.why: "You are responsible to uphold ethical standards while a student" is a general duty of ethical conduct. It fits P29 only partly because it is not about submitted work.
units.anchor: You are responsible to uphold ethical standards while a student
units.fit_note: General ethical-standards duty, not ownership of submitted work.

units.why: "It is your responsibility to check with your faculty about AI use in their course" makes the student responsible for learning each course's AI rule, so P78 (not P10, which is about asking when unsure).
units.anchor: It is your responsibility to check with your faculty about AI use in their course

units.why: "Be aware this may vary for each assignment" says AI rules can differ by assignment, so the decision sits at the assignment level (P04).
units.anchor: Be aware this may vary for each assignment

units.why: The "AI Assessment Scale" table sets four named levels of AI use (No AI, Plan, Collaborate, Create), which is the definition of P05.
units.anchor: AI Assessment Scale
units.policy: The university presents an AI Assessment Scale with four levels of GenAI use: No AI, Plan with AI, Collaborate with AI, Create with AI.

units.why: The "No AI" level says the task is done "independently without any GenAI assistance". It is the ban level of the scale; P01 is closest, but it applies per task, so a fit note.
units.anchor: The task is completed independently without any GenAI assistance
units.fit_note: A ban that applies only to tasks the instructor places at the No AI level, not by default.

units.why: The "Plan with AI" level allows GenAI for "brainstorming, outlining, or initial research" before the task. Brainstorming is P15.
units.anchor: GenAI may be used for pre-task activities such as brainstorming, outlining, or initial research
units.fit_note: Also allows outlining and initial research.

units.why: The "Collaborate with AI" level lets GenAI help complete the task by "creating a draft, providing feedback, and grammar edits". Writing support is P91; it also allows idea generation, so a fit note.
units.anchor: creating a draft, providing feedback, and grammar edits
units.policy: At the Collaborate with AI level, GenAI is used to help complete the task, like idea generation, creating a draft, providing feedback, and grammar edits.
units.fit_note: Also covers idea generation and helping complete the task, beyond editing.

units.why: The "Create with AI" level says GenAI "is used to complete an elements of the task", allowing AI-generated content for parts of a task. P16 (AI output under stated conditions); the condition is the instructor placing the task at this level.
units.anchor: GenAI is used to complete an elements of the task
units.fit_note: Does not state conditions such as caps or citation; the tier itself is the condition.

units.why: The checklist intro, "To better ensure your work is your own", says students should be able to answer yes to each statement; it ties the checklist to owning the work (P29).
units.anchor: To better ensure your work is your own, you should be able to confidently answer

units.why: "I have been permitted, by my faculty member, to use GenAI on this assignment" makes instructor permission a precondition for use, so P04.
units.anchor: I have been permitted, by my faculty member, to use GenAI on this assignment
units.fit_note: Frames instructor permission as a precondition checked by the student.

units.why: "I understand the way in which I am permitted to use GenAI on this assignment" requires the student to know the permitted use, so P78.
units.anchor: I understand the way in which I am permitted to use GenAI on this assignment

units.why: "I am using my own thoughts, words, and tone of voice" says the submitted work must be the student's own, so P29.
units.anchor: I am using my own thoughts, words, and tone of voice

units.why: "I have checked sources, and properly cited any facts, statistics, or quotes to the original author" asks students to check and cite the underlying sources. P31 (verify) is nearest; citing exceeds it.
units.anchor: properly cited any facts, statistics, or quotes to the original author
units.fit_note: Also requires citing facts, statistics and quotes to the original author.

units.why: "I have analyzed the GenAI output and identified false, biased, and inaccurate information" is a verify-and-critically-evaluate duty, so P31.
units.anchor: analyzed the GenAI output and identified false, biased, and inaccurate

units.why: "I have documented how I used GenAI and have cited it properly" requires documenting and citing AI use. P26 (document use) fits "documented how I used", but P24 (cite) is also touched; I chose P26 because documenting the use goes beyond a citation.
units.anchor: I have documented how I used GenAI and have cited it properly
units.fit_note: Also requires proper citation (P24), and does not say whether the documentation is submitted.

units.why: "I have not used confidential, protected, or copyrighted information" bars putting confidential or protected data into AI. P50 (protect confidential data) fits; the copyright part is P52, so a fit note.
units.anchor: I have not used confidential, protected, or copyrighted information
units.fit_note: Also covers copyrighted information (P52); does not say 'enter into AI' explicitly.

units.why: "I can explain all my findings and demonstrate full understanding of the assignment without the aid of GenAI" requires students to explain and defend their work, so P30.
units.anchor: I can explain all my findings and demonstrate full understanding

units.why: "I can prove what sources I used and how I verified the information" requires students to keep proof of sources and verification. P31 is nearest; proof of process is partly P26.
units.anchor: I can prove what sources I used and how I verified the information
units.fit_note: Requires being able to prove sources and verification steps, a documentation duty beyond verifying.

units.why: "doing it yourself imperfectly is the truest testament of learning" gives the learning reason for limiting AI: doing the work yourself builds skill (P41).
units.anchor: doing it yourself imperfectly is the truest testament of learning

notes: One included document, university layer. Several types fit only partly; fit notes record this. Source text has typos (for example 'slights edits', 'an elements') kept in anchors.
